newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's landless kill cattle to feed their hungry.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's landless kill cattle to feed their hungry.

text.p: Members of Brazil's Landless Movement (MST), who focus on the plight of rural life with invasions of private estates, were slaughtering cattle on a farm in southern Brazil for food, a state government official said on Thursday.

The Mato Grosso do Sul state official said 2,165 landless families who have been occupying a farm in Itaquirai since July, had slaughtered 42 cattle and threatened to kill more if the government did not deliver on its promise to supply food.

MST coordinator for Mato Grosso do Sul state, Osaney Pereira de Lima, said authorities promised to deliver 2,165 basic food baskets to the landless families if they left the farm and freed the 450 cattle they had captured upon occupying the property.
He said even though the families had released the cows the government held back the food because the people refused to leave the farm before the food arrived.
"This is not a new general strategy which the MST has adopted to pressure the government on land reform," Lima said. "It's just a measure taken by people who don't want to go hungry."
He said the meat would probably be enough to feed the 7,500 landless peasants until Friday, but he denied that there were plans to kill off more cattle for food.
Lima said state public security secretary Joaquim D'Assuncao de Sousa was in Brasilia to find a "peaceful" solution with the help of the federal government.
He said state officials for now were delaying sending in the police to resolve the dispute and clear the landless families from the property.
